instruction: In VS Code User settings, set the editor tab size to 4.

command: cd /home/user/Downloads && unzip -q vscodeEvalExtension.zip && code --install-extension vscodeEvalExtension/eval-0.0.1.vsix && rm -rf vscodeEvalExtension vscodeEvalExtension.zip

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (get_vscode_config) correctly reads /home/user/.config/Code/User/settings.json, which is the standard VS Code User settings file on Linux — matching the instruction's 'User settings' requirement.
The expected parameter handling is correct: get_rule returns config['rules'] = {"expected": {"editor.tabSize": 4}}, and check_json_settings accesses expected['expected'] to get {"editor.tabSize": 4}.
The metric checks exactly editor.tabSize == 4, which directly verifies the single requirement in the instruction.
Full instruction coverage: single-requirement task, single metric check — no missing steps.
Baseline resistance is confirmed: metadata states initial User settings are empty (no tabSize), so the evaluator will not trivially pass.
The getter uses the VS Code command palette ('Preferences: Open Settings (JSON)') before reading the file, ensuring the settings file is up-to-date and any pending writes are flushed.
The static validation warning about type annotation mismatch (expected: str vs actual Dict) is structural only and does not affect runtime correctness since Python does not enforce type hints.
